channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Will Paramount’s creation of Skydance test France’s cultural exception?
item.description: Skydance’s $110 billion creation tests whether France’s cultural exception can still compel a leveraged global media giant to fund, protect and prioritise French creativity, or merely treat it as a compliance cost.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV discharged from hospital, to return to Vatican
item.description: Pope Leo XIV was discharged from Rome’s Gemelli Polyclinic on Saturday after doctors deemed him fit to leave following surgery on his right lung.

item.title: Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say
item.description: Three children and one teacher are dead after a shooter forced his way into a Bend, Oregon, elementary school and opened fire, authorities said.

item.title: Perspective: Midterm money madness
item.description: Campaign ad spending has topped $10 billion this election cycle, as voters struggle to afford groceries and gas.

item.title: France faces day of cost-of-living protests
item.description: French authorities detained dozens on Saturday at the start of nationwide protests against the cost of living, in what is likely to be a key indicator of the social climate heading toward elections to replace President Emmanuel Macron. France 24's Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.

item.title: Iran live updates: Trump admin prepares options, including 'mother of all bombs'
item.description: A dozen people were killed Saturday during a "brutal" attack at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said.

item.title: Cameroonian journalist shot in Bamenda
item.description: Cameroonian journalist Ambe Macmillan is recovering in hospital after being shot in the legs by gunmen in the north-western city of Bamenda. A young woman was also killed as the attackers opened fire on mourners attending a wake. The shooting has renewed concerns about the dangers facing journalists in Cameroon's English-speaking regions, after years of conflict between government forces and separatist groups.

item.title: Man charged with murder after fatal assault at caravan park
item.description: A man has been charged with murder following a fatal assault at a caravan park in Clacton-on-Sea.

item.title: Uganda launches Ebola vaccine trial
item.description: The town of Masaka in southern Uganda is currently conducting a Phase 1 trial of a vaccine candidate against the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which is circulating in the region. There is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for this strain.

item.title: Decades after apartheid, South Africans seek justice for crimes of the past
item.description: More than three decades after the end of apartheid, families of victims of some of the worst crimes of South Africa's past are still fighting for justice. As survivors and perpetrators grow older, a new wave of legal efforts is seeking truth, accountability and reparations before it's too late.

item.title: Kenya reports third Ebola case, contact tracing continues
item.description: Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola, a relative of a man who died earlier this month after travelling from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The health ministry said the 65-year-old woman tested positive while in quarantine, where she has been since 5 October. The second patient, a 39-year-old man from the same family, is in a stable condition. Health officials say there is no evidence of community transmission, as both individuals were under quarantine. However, three contacts have yet to be traced. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.

item.title: Russia hails Trump waiving sanctions as 'historic'
item.description: Russia on Saturday hailed US President Donald Trump's move to waive new sanctions on it as "historic", as Ukraine worries he is taking Moscow's side in Europe's worst conflict since World War II.

item.title: Coastal homes burn as hot winds fuel California fires
item.description: A fast-moving fire fueled by high winds burned at least six homes in Southern California on Friday, engulfing expensive coastal properties and prompting thousands to evacuate.

item.title: Trump's new press secretary out after less than week
item.description: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was pushed out Friday after less than a week in the high-profile job following a series of blunders that added to distractions for her embattled boss, President Donald Trump.

item.title: Pope Leo returns to Vatican four days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV was released from the hospital on Saturday after lung cancer surgery. Doctors removed part of the 71-year-old's right lung last week to extract a cancerous tumour.

item.title: Water bills face £40 hike if sector is downgraded, industry chief warns
item.description: Water customers face having to pay an extra £40 a year to suppliers if the industry is hit by a fresh ratings downgrade, the head of the industry's main lobbying group has warned.

item.title: UK advises against all but essential travel to Saudi Arabia
item.description: The UK has advised against all but essential travel to Saudi Arabia after attacks by Yemen's Houthis in the region.

item.title: Trump says did not order curb to Starshield for Ukraine
item.description: Donald Trump said Friday he did not request a reduction in Starshield services for Ukraine, after tech billionaire Elon Musk insisted any limits on the SpaceX-operated communications system would ultimately have come from the US president.

item.title: Ligue 1: Paris Saint-Germain aim to build on recent progress at Strasbourg
item.description: Fresh from their impressive 4-2 Champions League win on Manchester City’s home turf on Wednesday, PSG travel to Strasbourg on Saturday in Ligue 1. They aim to secure a fourth consecutive league win and maintain their growing momentum ahead of Tuesday's Champions League showdown with Barcelona.

item.title: Pope Leo leaves hospital after lung cancer surgery, the Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo has left hospital, four days after his lung cancer surgery.

item.title: Zelensky drums up European backing as Trump ties slump
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged EU leaders Friday to keep financing Kyiv's fight with nearly $80 billion more next year, as he insisted he was standing up for his country amid a fresh row with US President Donald Trump.

item.title: Trump waives new Russia sanctions as Ukraine ties slump
item.description: President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions and tariffs targeting Russia's energy revenues, marking a new low in Washington's ties with war-torn Ukraine. Our correspondent Gulliver Cragg tells us more.

item.title: Students, trade unions and Yellow Vests set to protest across France
item.description: Tens of thousands of ⁠people are expected to ​protest across France on Saturday, as students, trade unionists and remnants of the Yellow Vest movement join forces to demonstrate against high prices and ​the country's fraying social model.

item.title: No Kings turns its focus to voting this weekend. Here's what we know
item.description: The coalition behind nationwide anti-Trump protests is shifting its strategies this weekend to focus on voter turnout. Organizers say Saturday's events are a nonpartisan effort to get people to the polls.

item.title: Sidewalk sleepers: They have nowhere else to stay while a loved one is in the hospital
item.description: Patients travel miles to be treated at public hospitals in Delhi. Those in need get financial aid for their care. But for overnight accommodations, families are often on their own — and on the street.

item.title: Weddings are expensive. How about a grocery store cake?
item.description: About a third of couples are willing to save money on cake and dessert, according to the wedding-planning site Zola.

item.title: WATCH: Rhode Island farmer sets new record for world's biggest pumpkin
item.description: David Muir reports on the new world record for heaviest pumpkin, which weighs 3,156 pounds – smashing the previous record of 2,856 pounds set merely a week ago.

item.title: Heathrow expansion would boost growth, chancellor says
item.description: Chancellor John Healey has shown support for expanding Heathrow Airport after Prime Minister Andy Burnham refused to back plans for a third runway.

item.title: Two dead after light aircraft crash
item.description: An 80-year-old man and a 16-year-old boy have died after a light aircraft crashed in Scotland, police have said.

item.title: Three men sentenced to more than 158 years in jail for murders of surfers​
item.description: Three men have been sentenced to 158 years and nine months each for the murders of two Australian brothers and their American friend.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis claim responsibility for fresh missile strike on Aden airport
item.description: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed responsibility after two missiles struck Aden International Airport on Friday, saying they had targeted a weapons depot as well as a military command headquarters. The Aden Security Department said a Yemenia Airways flight bound for Cairo had been preparing for takeoff when the attack took place.

item.title: Trump signs order waiving Graham Act sanctions on Russia
item.description: The new sanctions and tariffs were set to take effect in two days.

item.title: Live: Tens of thousands join protests across France, clashes reported in several cities
item.description: French police used tear gas and batons to try to drive protesters from the streets in Paris, Marseille and Lyon as demonstrators staged unsanctioned marches and tried to block traffic with impromptu barricades Saturday. Tens of thousands of people are expected to demonstrate across France as students, trade union members and remnants of the Yellow Vest movement join forces to protest rising cost of living. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Trump administration threatens to prosecute local California election workers
item.description: The DOJ sued over claims the state hasn't purge noncitizens from voter rolls.

item.title: WATCH: Authorities: Fatal alligator attack in Winter Garden, Florida
item.description: Police say the man was fishing along the shoreline at a park when he was attacked and killed by an alligator.

item.title: Bipartisan group of senators want answers on Starlink disruptions in Ukraine
item.description: The lawmakers say American personnel were endangered in attacks on Ukraine.

item.title: Georgia's Senate and governor races test Trump's political influence
item.description: Trump plays a significant role in Georgia's races, with Democrats working to tie their GOP opponents to Trump’s unpopular policies on the economy and war with Iran.

item.title: WATCH: Hero who stopped Oregon elementary school shooting suspect identified
item.description: ABC News contributor Don Mihalek discusses the bystander credited with stopping the suspected gunman and ongoing investigations.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Teacher fought with Oregon gunman before parent shot suspect
item.description: A teacher threw her phone at the teenage gunman who killed four people in a school shooting in Oregon before tackling and fighting with him, police have said.

item.title: Zelensky fears Trump 'will continue' to lift Russia sanctions
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that he feared his US counterpart Donald Trump "will continue" lifitng sanctions on Russia. Zelensky's relationship with Trump deteriorated after the Washington eased sanctions on Moscow as part of a diesel-supply deal, despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine.

item.title: KENYA CONFIRMS THIRD EBOLA CASE
item.description: In tonight's programme, Kenya confirms a third case of Ebola, a relative of a man who died earlier this month after travelling from DR Congo. Also,Cameroonian journalist Ambe Macmillan is recovering in hospital after being shot in the legs by gunmen in Bamenda. And we meet Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama... And finally, we meet Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama, who digs deep into his country's colonial and industrial past to lay new creative foundations for generations to come.

item.title: 'Finish what we started': After student protests, France braces for return of the Yellow Vests
item.description: An online movement against rising fuel prices has gained momentum ahead of planned nationwide demonstrations on October 17 with former Yellow Vest figures set to join the protests in support of high-school students. Some are drawing parallels between the latest action and the 2018 cost-of-living protests that rattled President Emmanuel Macron's first term in office.

item.title: Clashes grip Tirana as Albanian PM blames 'foreign hands' for mounting unrest
item.description: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Friday blamed the involvement of “foreign hands” for escalating protests, which he said are aimed at hindering Albania's bid to join the European Union. Thousands of demonstrators have taken to the streets of Albania's capital since Tuesday, demanding Rama’s resignation and denouncing university conditions and high tuition fees.

item.title: How Elon Musk is bankrolling GOP’s hopes in Texas Senate race
item.description: New campaign finance filings show the major role billionaire Elon Musk is playing in bankrolling GOP efforts against Democrat James Talarico in Texas.

item.title: Trump Vs Zelensky, From the Screen to the Streets, Gen Z protests from Paris to Dehli
item.description: In India, the Cockroach movement felt the crushing boot of the state this week. Thousands of Gen Z protesters were rounded up and detained in sports stadiums and community halls turned into makeshift detention centres, while the movement’s founder, Abhijeet Dipke, was arrested on arrival. A mass demonstration over alleged voter fraud was effectively crushed before it could begin.And Abdijeet has been detained again todayNarendra Modi’s government says the measures were necessary to protect civilians in the capital. But he now faces accusations of choosing repression over democracy, with the UN Human Rights Office urging authorities to respect the right to peaceful assembly. It’s been a week of blame games and accusations of betrayal in Ukraine with President Zelensky speaking of his personal hurt at President Trump’s decision to make a diesel deal with the Kremlin ahead of the US Mid term elections calling it “weak”, suggesting Trump had chosen, “the other side”. item.title: New York Democrats want parking lot owners to ban ICE from their properties
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and top New York Democrats are urging private parking lot owners to block federal immigration officers from using their properties

item.title: 'US tilting toward Russia: Europeans are standing more and more solidly with Zelensky'
item.description: As transatlantic relations confront renewed geopolitical uncertainty, former Estonian President Toomas Hendrik Ilves delivers a pointed assessment of Washington's shifting approach to Russia's war on Ukraine and the profound implications for European security. At the heart of his analysis lies a fundamental question: can Europe develop the political unity, strategic independence and military capabilities necessary to defend its interests in an increasingly unpredictable international order? Ilves response: "If there's any time for Europe to begin to act as Europe and not as being strictly self-interested, then this is the time for it."

item.title: WATCH: Nat Geo's 'Moment on the Earth' spotlights the wonders of elephants
item.description: National Geographic shares a closer look at elephants, including how they can eat up to 18 hours a day and even use their trunks to "hug." "Secrets of the Elephants" is streaming now.

item.title: Trump's press secretary responds after leaving role days after taking job
item.description: Katie Zacharia has left her role as White House press secretary a week after being appointed, saying "it was an honor to work for" Donald Trump.

item.title: Four dead as Istanbul suffers worst floods in 80 years
item.description: At least four people have died after Istanbul suffered its worst floods in more than 80 years, Turkish officials have said.

item.title: Sally Rooney's books no longer sold in UK over support for banned pro-Palestinian group
item.description: Irish novelist Sally ⁠Rooney's books will ​no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties ​to support Palestine Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney and her publisher said on Wednesday. The bestselling author, known for novels including "Normal People" and "Conversations with ​Friends", has ‌been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action, including after ⁠it was proscribed by the British government under terrorism laws last year.

item.title: Trump administration accused of fast-tracking migrant children's asylum cases
item.description: Immigrant advocacy groups have sued the Trump administration to stop what they call a "cruel and unlawful scheme" to fast-track migrant children's asylum cases.

item.title: WATCH: Aboard USS George Washington as tensions rise in the Middle East
item.description: ABC News is aboard the USS George Washington near the Strait of Hormuz with rare front-line access as President Donald Trump weighs expanded operations against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

item.title: What the Pope said to Putin in call days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: The Pope spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday and urged a truce with Ukraine as he continued his recovery from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said.

item.title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia says she did not pass bar exam
item.description: Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer; Trump called her "an attorney."

item.title: WATCH: Elon Musk unveils Tesla's new Roadster, and it can fly
item.description: Using SpaceX rocket technology, the sports car climbed a curved ramp and hurled itself to a controlled landing.

item.title: Drugs fuelling 'horrific' events seen in Waterford, says Irish justice minister
item.description: People who take illegal drugs are "supporting the horrific events we saw in Waterford", Irish justice minister Jim O'Callaghan has said.

item.title: Madeleine McCann prime suspect could face new rape trial
item.description: The prime suspect in the Madeleine McCann case could face a new rape trial after German prosecutors launched a legal bid to overturn his acquittal on a string of sex charges, unrelated to the missing British girl.

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks, Broncos face off in Thursday night NFL matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Omar Ruiz previews the Seahawks-Broncos showdown in Denver, including how Seattle’s top-ranked defense could challenge Bo Nix and whether Sam Darnold can bounce back after two interceptions.

item.title: WATCH: Rising number of young adults living with parents
item.description: ABC News’ Juju Chang reports on the growing trend of “boomerang kids” returning to live with their parents amid housing costs and financial concerns.

item.title: WATCH: DIY Halloween costumes for this year’s viral trends
item.description: Lori Bergamotto shares easy, last-minute DIY Halloween costume ideas inspired by the people and pop culture moments that made headlines this year.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir hears from Georgia firefighters who helped deliver 15 puppies
item.description: Firefighters in Cobb County answered an emergency call to help a veterinary hospital deliver 15 puppies after a rescue dog came to the local animal hospital.

item.title: WATCH: Aggressive great white shark seen off Southern California coast
item.description: Experts say the shark could be hunting for seals.

item.title: WATCH: Measles, GLP-1s and anti-aging: How to protect your health
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi discusses the resurgence of measles, the potential health benefits of GLP-1 drugs and what we can do now to prevent disease and live longer.

item.title: WATCH: How to navigate rising prices this holiday season
item.description: ABC News’ Elizabeth Schulze reports on what to know about the latest inflation report and prices this coming holiday season.
